sentences.ko: 근데 우리 부모님한테는 그쯤 되니까 '어, 그래, 뭐 하루 이틀 일이냐' 이런 느낌이었지.
sentences.text: But to my parents, by then it was like, yeah, right, well, what else is new?

alts.text: My parents were basically like, eh, so what, nothing new.
By that point, my parents simply did not find it surprising anymore.

sentences.note: **what else is new** 는 '늘 그렇지 뭐, 새삼스럽지도 않아' 하고 시큰둥하게 받을 때 씁니다. 남이 보인 반응을 그대로 옮겨 말할 때는 **it was like** 로 시작하면 자연스럽습니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends

sentences.ko: 아 진짜, 내가 이걸 고민하고 있다는 게 말이 되냐.
sentences.text: Oh god, I can't believe I'm even considering this.

alts.text: Wow, am I seriously thinking about this?
I am honestly surprised that I am considering this at all.

sentences.note: **even considering** 은 '원래라면 고민할 거리도 아닌데 내가 지금 이걸 고민하고 있네' 하는 느낌입니다. 끌리는데 하면 안 될 것 같은 제안을 받았을 때 혼잣말처럼 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends

sentences.ko: 우리는 그냥, 네가 여자친구 맞춰 주느라 너무 많은 걸 포기하는 것 같아서 그래.
sentences.text: We we just we just think that you're having to sacrifice a whole lot to make her happy.

alts.text: Feels like you're giving up a ton just to keep her happy.
It seems to us that you are sacrificing a great deal in order to make her happy.

sentences.note: **we just think** 는 친구에게 듣기 싫은 말을 조심스럽게 꺼낼 때 앞에 붙이는 말입니다. **a whole lot** 은 a lot 을 더 힘줘 말하는 구어입니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends

sentences.ko: 야, 그거 입고 가는 건 진짜 아닌 것 같다.
sentences.text: Dude, I really don't think you should be wearing that.

alts.text: Bro, that's not a good look.
Honestly, I do not believe you should wear that.

sentences.note: **I really don't think you should** 는 '하지 마' 대신 부드럽게 말리는 표현입니다. 친구 옷차림이나 결정에 한마디 할 때 딱 맞습니다. **Dude** 는 친한 친구를 부를 때 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 그럼, 본격적으로 시작하기 전에 혹시 하고 싶은 말 있어?
sentences.text: So, is is there anything you want to say, you know, before it all starts?

alts.text: Anything you wanna say before we kick things off?
Would you like to say anything before everything begins?

sentences.note: **before it all starts** 는 결혼식·발표·여행처럼 큰일이 시작되기 직전에 씁니다. 중간의 **you know** 는 말을 고르며 잠깐 숨 돌릴 때 끼우는 말버릇입니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends

sentences.ko: 이 안약 일주일 동안 하루에 세 번씩 넣으세요. 그러면 다시 멀쩡해질 거예요.
sentences.text: I want you to take these drops three times a day for a week and you'll be as good as new.

alts.text: Use these drops three times a day for a week, and you'll be totally fine.
Please use these drops three times daily for one week, and you will make a full recovery.

sentences.note: **as good as new**는 아팠던 몸이나 고장 났던 물건이 완전히 원래대로 돌아왔을 때 써요. **I want you to**는 의사나 선생님이 해야 할 일을 부드럽게 일러 줄 때 자주 하는 말이에요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends

sentences.ko: 아니, 누가 잘못했는지는 너무 뻔한 것 같은데.
sentences.text: No, I think it's very obvious who's wrong here.

alts.text: Come on, it's pretty clear who messed up.
Actually, I believe it is quite clear who is at fault in this situation.

sentences.note: 말다툼에서 상대편 잘못이라고 콕 집을 때 **who's wrong here**라고 해요. 여기서 here는 장소가 아니라 '이 일에서'라는 뜻이에요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 저기, 잠깐 저쪽에서 얘기 좀 할 수 있을까?
sentences.text: Uh, can I talk to you for a second over there?

alts.text: Got a sec? Let's step over there.
Excuse me, may I speak with you over there for a moment?

sentences.note: 남들 앞에서 하기 곤란한 말이 있어서 누군가를 따로 불러낼 때 **talk to you for a second**라고 해요. 정말 1초라는 뜻이 아니라 '잠깐'이에요.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.text: This is harder than I thought it would be.

alts.text: Man, this is way tougher than I figured.
I must admit, this is more difficult than I had expected.

sentences.note: 해 보니 예상보다 힘들 때 **harder than I thought it would be**라고 해요. harder 자리에 easier, better 같은 말을 넣어서 그대로 쓸 수 있어요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 그냥 그 사람이랑 만나면서 좋은 점이랑 나쁜 점을 한번 따져 보는 게 어때?
sentences.text: Why don't you just weigh out the good stuff about the relationship against the bad stuff?

alts.text: Just think about the good and the bad, you know?
Perhaps you should weigh the positive aspects of the relationship against the negative ones.

sentences.note: 고민하는 친구한테 가볍게 권할 때 **Why don't you just**로 말을 꺼내요. 장점·단점을 말할 때 회화에서는 **the good stuff**처럼 stuff를 붙여 편하게 말하는 경우가 많아요.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends
